discovery: Quantum control of macroscopic mechanical motion: cavity optomechanics and quantum acoustics

nominees.name: Andrew N. Cleland
nominees.affiliation: Pritzker School of Molecular Engineering, University of Chicago, USA

nominees.name: Markus Aspelmeyer
nominees.affiliation: University of Vienna and IQOQI Vienna, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

nominees.name: Tobias J. Kippenberg
nominees.affiliation: Ecole Polytechnique Federale de Lausanne (EPFL), Switzerland

motivation: The nominees brought mechanical objects containing billions of atoms into the quantum regime. Cleland and co-workers (Nature 2010) coupled a superconducting qubit to a micromechanical resonator. They prepared its quantum ground state and exchanged single phonons with it, which was the first quantum control of a man-made mechanical object. Aspelmeyer and Kippenberg founded cavity optomechanics. Their work established radiation-pressure sideband cooling, strong optomechanical coupling and ground-state cooling with laser light, together with squeezing, entanglement and quantum-limited measurement of motion. Aspelmeyer later extended ground-state control to levitated nanoparticles, which opens tests of quantum mechanics at large mass and of gravity. Together these advances created a new field that tests macroscopic quantum coherence directly. It also provides practical tools: quantum transducers linking microwave and optical photons, phonon-based quantum memories and precision force sensors. These are central to hybrid quantum technologies.
